words: Light moves in straight lines until it hits something or passes into something new. That is why shadows have sharp edges.
When light bounces off a surface. Mirrors, calm water, and shiny metal reflect light.
When a material soaks up light energy instead of bouncing it back. Dark colors absorb more light and turn it into heat.
When light bends as it passes from one material into another, like from water into air.
The rubbing of two surfaces against each other. Friction changes motion energy into heat energy.
When heat energy moves from a warmer thing to a cooler thing, like a hot pan warming your soup.
The outside of an object. Smooth, shiny surfaces reflect more light. Dark surfaces absorb more.

parts.title: How Light Travels
parts.html:
Light travels in a straight line until it hits something or passes into something new, like water. That is why a flashlight makes a straight beam, and why your hand in the beam makes a shadow.

When light hits a surface, it can pass through, bounce off, bend, or be soaked up. What happens depends on the material.

parts.title: Reflection, Refraction, and Absorption
parts.html:
Reflection is when light bounces off a surface. Mirrors, calm water, and shiny metal reflect light well. Refraction is when light bends as it passes from water into air. It makes a straw in water look broken.

Absorption is when a material soaks up light. Dark colors absorb more light and turn it into heat, so a black shirt gets hotter in the sun than a white one.

parts.title: Friction Makes Heat
parts.html:
Heat doesn't only come from light. When two things rub together, friction changes motion energy into heat energy. Rub your hands together fast, and they warm up.

Bike and car brakes press against moving wheels to slow them down. All that rubbing makes the brakes hot.

wow.title: A Mirror on the Moon
wow.alt: A flat box of small round mirrors sitting on the gray dust of the Moon, with the lunar lander behind it
wow.caption: The laser mirror left on the Moon by Apollo 11, 1969
wow.html:
In 1969, Apollo 11 astronauts left a special mirror on the Moon. Scientists on Earth still shine laser light at it.

The light travels in a straight line to the Moon, bounces off the mirror, and comes back, in about 2½ seconds round trip!
wow.insetCap: A green laser beam aimed at the Moon from NASA Goddard, Maryland.

keyIdea: Light travels in a straight line until it hits something or passes into something new. Then it can pass through, bend (refraction), bounce off (reflection), or be soaked up (absorption). Dark surfaces absorb more light and turn it into heat; light, shiny surfaces reflect more. Friction, when things rub together, changes motion energy into heat energy.

quiz.q: What happens when light hits a mirror?

options.t: The light is reflected: it bounces off the surface
options.ok: 🌲 Correct! Mirrors are smooth and shiny, so they reflect light. The light bounces off the surface.

options.t: The light is absorbed: it is taken in by the mirror
options.miss: Think about what you see in a mirror. If the light were absorbed, could you see your reflection?

options.t: The light passes through the mirror
options.miss: Think about what you see in a mirror. If the light went through, could you see your reflection?

quiz.q: Why does a dark-colored surface feel warmer in the sun than a light-colored surface?

options.t: Dark surfaces reflect more light energy
options.miss: Think about what absorption means. When light is absorbed, where does the energy go?

options.t: Dark surfaces absorb more light energy and change it into heat
options.ok: 🌲 Yes! Dark surfaces absorb more light energy. That absorbed energy turns into heat, making the surface feel warmer.

options.t: Dark surfaces create more friction
options.miss: Think about what absorption means. When light is absorbed, where does the energy go?

quiz.q: A student rubs two sticks together quickly and they start to feel warm. What is causing the heat?

options.t: Reflection of light
options.miss: The sticks are being rubbed together. What happens when two surfaces rub against each other?

options.t: Absorption of sound energy
options.miss: The sticks are being rubbed together. What happens when two surfaces rub against each other?

options.t: Friction between the two surfaces
options.ok: 🌲 Exactly! Rubbing two surfaces together makes friction, and friction changes motion energy into heat.

partA.title: Light interaction chart
partA.do: Read each one. Pick the best answer, or type your answer.

items.q: Mirror: does light mostly reflect or absorb? How do you know?

options.t: It reflects. You can see yourself in it.
options.ok: Yes. A mirror bounces light back to your eyes, so you see your reflection.

options.t: It absorbs. The light disappears into it.
options.miss: If a mirror soaked up light, could you see yourself in it?

options.t: Light goes straight through it, like a window.
options.miss: Can you see through a mirror to the wall behind it?

items.q: White paper in the sun: does light mostly reflect or absorb? What happens to its temperature?

options.t: It mostly absorbs light, so it gets very hot.
options.miss: Light colors bounce back most of the light. Think about the white shirt.

options.t: It bends the light, like water.
options.miss: Bending happens when light goes from water into air. What does white paper do?

options.t: It mostly reflects light, so it stays cooler.
options.ok: Yes. White paper bounces back most of the light, so it stays cooler.

items.q: Black paper in the sun: does light mostly reflect or absorb? What happens to its temperature?

options.t: It mostly reflects light, so it stays cool.
options.miss: Dark colors soak up most of the light. Think about the black shirt.

options.t: It mostly absorbs light, so it gets warmer.
options.ok: Yes. Black paper soaks up most of the light, and the light turns into heat.

options.t: It makes its own light.
options.miss: Paper doesn't glow. What does it do with sunlight?
